summary:
Star Sailors is a free, fully narrated web game that teaches the real history of spaceflight, then turns players into mission designers. It runs in any browser on a phone, tablet or computer, with no download, no login and no cost.

Captain Nova, an astronaut guide, leads players through seven playable chapters: Freedom 7, Explorer 1, Apollo 11, Apollo 13, Voyager 1, the Mars rovers and the James Webb Space Telescope. Each chapter opens with real NASA photos and film, then hands over the controls: build Freedom 7, land the Eagle through the 1202 alarm, steer Apollo 13 home, fly Ingenuity and unfold Webb.

For the Space Mission Design Game challenge, our special mode, Test Your Knowledge, lets players earn credits through quizzes, pick a destination and spend those credits on a spacecraft, power, radio, shielding, instruments and a rocket. Their design then faces NASA-style shake, thermal and deployment tests before it launches, lands and does science, ending in a mission report.

Every fact comes from NASA's open data. With narration, bigger text, calm motion and a relaxed mode, any kid, anywhere, can learn how real missions are designed and try one.
details:
Star Sailors is a free, browser-based educational game that takes players through the history of space exploration, from the first astronauts to today’s telescopes, and then lets them design a mission of their own. It runs on any phone, tablet or computer with no download, no login and no cost. It is designed for children first, while staying engaging for adults and space enthusiasts. Captain Nova, an astronaut guide, leads the player through seven playable chapters: Freedom 7, Explorer 1, Apollo 11, Apollo 13, Voyager 1, the Mars rovers and the James Webb Space Telescope. Each chapter opens with real NASA photos and film, then hands the player the controls in hands-on minigames: building Freedom 7, landing the Eagle through the 1202 alarm, steering Apollo 13 home by the Earth, flying Ingenuity and unfolding Webb in deep space. In the special mode, Test Your Knowledge, players answer quizzes to earn credits, choose a destination and spend those credits on a spacecraft, power, radio, shielding, instruments and a rocket strong enough to lift it all. Their ship then faces NASA-style shake, thermal and deployment tests before it launches, cruises, lands and does science, ending in a mission report with stars, a grade and a chart to share. Every fact, mission and number comes from NASA’s open data (nasa.gov, science.nasa.gov, NASA Space Place and NASA+), with photos and footage from the NASA Image and Video Library.

Star Sailors is built so anyone can play, regardless of age, device or ability. It runs in any browser, and a “sharp graphics” option can be switched off so it stays smooth on low-end devices. Every mission is explained in short, clear language with no jargon, so children can follow along while adults and experts still find depth. Captain Nova reads every line aloud at the speed the player chooses. Text can be made bigger, motion can be calmed down, and a relaxed mode makes every minigame more forgiving, with hints and landing help when players need them. The minigames use simple taps, clicks, swipes or the keyboard, with on-screen guidance at every step. Information comes through film, narration, text and hands-on play together, so players can learn in the way that suits them best.

It can be played now at: https://nasa-hackathon.pages.dev
